definition: A long-range electrostatics mechanism intended to recover interpretable latent charges from energies/forces without explicitly supervising charges or running charge equilibration, while coupling short-range learned interactions with Ewald-style long-range treatment.
assumptions: latent charges should be inferable from data when electrostatics dominate
global electrostatic interactions require nonlocal treatment beyond short-range cutoffs
charge-state metadata may be needed when identical local structures map to different energies
invariants: long-range electrostatic contribution should depend on all atoms, not only local neighbors
derived charges should support interpretable electrostatic observables
benchmark analyses must preserve charge-state distinctions
non_negotiable_structural_steps: compare a local/short-range baseline against an electrostatics-aware model or analytic descriptor
evaluate charge recovery or charge-proxy fidelity on the random_charges benchmark
evaluate separation-dependent behavior on charged dimers

this_workspace_fidelity_plan.exact_end_to_end_LES_reproduction: not feasible from available workspace alone because the paper/method implementation is not provided and datasets are limited
this_workspace_fidelity_plan.faithful_minimal_benchmark: use analytic electrostatic descriptors and simple regressors as a benchmark-faithful approximation to test the named scientific claims
